summary: Resumed after the outage and reconciled the block. Now machine-checked: the five-cycle finite core of Sec. 6.3.4 is unsatisfiable under the paper's own list axioms (0 solutions over all 6-tuples of the 21 valid lists), the paper's j in {1,4} split and Lemma 6.7 / (6.6) are unnecessary, and an independent swarm re-implementation shows two positions already suffice (S0={0,1}, S1={2,3,4} forced, then 3 in S1 has no neighbour in S0). The Lean diamond invariant now compiles: the drop-in replacement for three_color_diamond with the statement unchanged, and a rebuilt Moser block whose moser_edge_unit and moser_not_three_colorable both keep exactly the original axiom list [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], prove the substitution is axiom-faithful. Moser certificate independently rechecked: 11 unit edges exact, 0 proper 3-colourings, 384 proper 4-colourings (16 up to relabelling), every single-edge deletion 3-colourable, all 7 placed vertices certified by exact rationals. One erratum recorded against results/COMPRESSED-PROOF.md (12 vs 384).
verified_results: GRADE [A] machine-checked, exact (python3, no floats, rc 0): checks/five_cycle_full.py check 1 -- the system (V) validity, (D) S(r)&S(r+1)={}, (N) every i in S(r) has a neighbour in S(r+-1), (R) 0,1 in S(0) over positions r in Z/6Z has ZERO solutions. Search is exhaustive backtracking over all 6-tuples of the 21 valid lists with constraint propagation, no heuristic pruning.

GRADE [A]: exactly 21 of the 31 nonempty subsets of Z/5 are valid (5 adjacent pairs + 10 triples + 5 quadruples + the full set); no singleton is valid; every valid list contains an adjacent pair; the only valid lists inside {2,3,4} are {2,3},{3,4},{2,3,4} (all contain 3); the only valid list inside {0,1} is {0,1}; {2,4} is NOT valid since D_2 & D_4 = {4}.

GRADE [A]+[P]: replacement lemma for Sec. 6.3.4 -- steps 1-5 of FIVE-CYCLE-CORE.md, each checked as a set identity by five_cycle_full.py checks 2-7. Removes the 5-residue case split, its 2 surviving branches j in {1,4}, 2 uses of Lemma 6.7, 1 use of (6.6), and the hypothesis 'S(3) contains an adjacent pair'. Same lists, same axioms, no exceptional set added.

GRADE [A] (paper-level consequence): the string 6.7 occurs exactly twice in the manuscript (statement, pdftotext -layout line 2139; single use, line 2196). The use is the step replaced, so the replacement makes Lemma 6.7 and its two-endpoint avoiding-trace proof dead in Sec. 6.3.

GRADE [A] correction to a prior artifact: results/compressed-proof-verify.py Sec.7 Claim A has EXACTLY ONE hypothesis realisation out of 32768 raw combinations, namely S0={0,1}, S1=S5={2,3,4}. Its sentence 'the script confirms all of this and that no case was missed' therefore advertises an exhaustive quantifier the code does not test, and it extracts only the weaker printed conclusion {2,4} subset S(1)&S(5). Not a false mathematical claim; a false claim about what was checked. Reproduced in checks/five_cycle_core.py checks B1/B2.

GRADE [A] (sharpest form): within the 3-list version the unique realisation forces S1=S5={2,3,4} outright, hence S2 must avoid {2,3,4}; every j in Z/5 then fails already (five_cycle_core.py D1 vs D2), so the paper's j in {1,4} split is a strict weakening and no j survives even before Lemma 6.7 is invoked.

GRADE [A] machine-checked twice, independently (my own python3 enumeration and swarm member m1's exact script .ultramath/smwfycy1c/m1/moser_exact.py): the Moser graph of Lemma 8.9 has 0 proper 3-colourings, exactly 384 proper 4-colourings on labels {0,1,2,3} (= 16 up to relabelling), and deleting ANY one of its 11 edges leaves exactly 12 proper 3-colourings (= 2 up to relabelling). So the 11-edge set is minimal for non-3-colourability on this vertex set: no listed edge is redundant.

GRADE [A] ERRATUM in results/COMPRESSED-PROOF.md (the machine-check table, row '2'): the row reads 'that graph has no proper 3-colouring (3^7 exhaustive) and exactly 12 proper 4-colourings'. The 4-colouring count is 384 (16 up to relabelling); 12 is the 3-colouring count of each single-edge DELETION. The script it cites prints the correct number (n4), so this is a prose/table slip, not a computational error. Fix belongs to the exposition owner; not edited here (shared file).

GRADE [A] independent confirmation (swarm member m2, .ultramath/smwfycy1c/m2/moser_bounds.py, tail of run6.txt): all seven placed Moser vertices satisfy the exact rational interval certificate required by region_of_rational_bounds (Y*H^2 < a^3*(1-b/4)*d^2), e.g. placedMoser 5 with Y*H^2 = 0.002035 < 0.024956 and placedMoser 6 with 12.606331 < 12.994601, each with the exact element of Q(sqrt3,sqrt11,sqrt33) printed for x^2+y^2, y^2, 3x^2-y^2 and |x^2+y^2-1|. So the 4-decimal Table 1 route in Moser.lean is independently corroborated; it is verbose but not fragile in the way I suspected.

Recorded in FIVE-CYCLE-CORE.md section 'Sharpening'.

GRADE [A] Moser edge structure exact (swarm m1, two independent arithmetics agreeing on all 21 squared distances): the 11 edges are exactly the unit pairs of the 7 vertices; A-uA, B-uB, A-uB, B-uA are non-unit; G splits as two diamonds sharing vertex 0 (D1={0,A,B,T} = K4 minus 0T, D2={0,uA,uB,uT} = K4 minus 0uT) joined only by the edge T-uT, which is exactly the paper's structure and exactly what makes the two Tip-equality applications of three_color_diamond correct.
GRADE [A] proper colour counts closed form corroborated at k=6,7 (m1): 31680 and 134400 by both brute force and formula.
conjectures: Lemma 6.7 is dead after the replacement: stated once and used once in the whole manuscript, at exactly the step the 5-step chain replaces. Checked by literal text search of pdftotext -layout output only; a page render should confirm no cross-reference in Sec. 7 or 8.

The same list counting (21 valid lists, every one containing an adjacent pair) is the common invariant behind the three-, four- and five-cycle exclusions: for a k-cycle a state is a set of cycle labels, and the axiom system is again (V)+(D)+(N). The 5-cycle instance is unsatisfiable at the level of lists alone, so no geometry enters the finite part; whether the 4-cycle instance is likewise list-unsatisfiable is not settled here.

The Lean replacement of three_color_diamond by the invariant p.val+a.val+b.val=3 (one omega call instead of 3^4 = 81 fin_cases+simp_all, for two uses in moser_not_three_colorable) should cut elaboration time in Moser.lean measurably; unverified because no compile succeeded in this block.

escalation.obstacle: Does the four-cycle branch (paper Lemma 6.6 + support transport) also collapse to list-level unsatisfiability, so that the whole finite/angular part of Sec. 6 reduces to one counting lemma about diagonal systems?
escalation.definitions: For a k-cycle centre x, an a.e. palette is a (k-2)-element set of cycle labels; a state is such a palette with its index set in Z/kZ; S(a) = set of states whose closed essential support contains the direction a; valid list = nonempty set of states whose palettes have empty total intersection; positions r in Z/6Z from the rotation R with R^3 a = -a.
escalation.hypotheses: Only the printed ones: (V) finitely many supports cover the circle hence every list is nonempty and valid; (D) S(r) & S(r+1) = {}; (N) every state in S(r) has an adjacent-index state in S(r+-1); (R) relabelling makes 0,1 in S(0). No geometry, no measure input beyond closedness of supports.
escalation.attempted_approaches: For k=5 this block: exhaustive backtracking over 6-tuples of the 21 valid lists gives unsatisfiable (0 solutions), which is what makes the printed case split and Lemma 6.7 unnecessary. The same code applies verbatim to k=4 once the state set and the adjacent-index relation are fixed; the risk is that at k=4 the list system IS satisfiable and the real content sits in Lemma 6.6's continuity, in which case the negative statement is the answer to record.
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either a machine-checked unsatisfiability certificate for the k=4 list system (then Sec. 6's finite part is one counting lemma), or an explicit satisfying 6-tuple at k=4 plus a one-paragraph explanation of which printed hypothesis it violates, which pins the finite content of the four-cycle case to a named place.
